subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw define first-class browser-plugin config/API for per-profile proxy and per-agent/subagent browser binding, or keep this to external orchestration, remote CDP, or multiple gateway setups until broader proxy and session-ownership designs land?
rationale: The requested feature adds public config and security-sensitive browser egress/session semantics that automation cannot choose safely from code inspection alone.

options.title: Design first-class browser contract
options.body: Specify and then implement the browser plugin/core contract for proxy secrets, SSRF policy, redaction, agent defaults, and subagent inheritance before accepting a code change.

options.title: Split into existing narrower issues
options.body: Use #60035 for proxy policy and #85672 for subagent browser ownership while keeping this issue as the umbrella until both slices are resolved.

options.title: Defer to external orchestration
options.body: Document supported external approaches such as remote CDP, multiple gateways, or browser orchestration tools and avoid adding new core/browser config for now.

recommendation.title: Design first-class browser contract
recommendation.body: Specify and then implement the browser plugin/core contract for proxy secrets, SSRF policy, redaction, agent defaults, and subagent inheritance before accepting a code change.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of browser plugin boundaries and runtime seam refactors touched by this request.
